args.question: What changes are needed in a setup to use Gram anchoring?
args.head: Integrating Gram Anchoring Into Existing Pipelines

args.brief: A diagram showing the additions for Gram anchoring: the active student network, the calculation of the student's Gram matrix, the storage of an older model checkpoint as a frozen Gram teacher, the down-sampling step, the anchor Gram matrix, and the Gram loss that constrains the student's patch relationships to those of the older model.

spec.head: Integrating Gram Anchoring Into Existing Pipelines
body: Gram anchoring prevents dense feature collapse in long training runs. Instead of forcing individual patch embeddings to match, it penalizes differences in patch similarity matrices.
The student processes global crops at standard resolution. A frozen checkpoint, the Gram teacher, processes the same crops at twice the resolution before its feature map is down-sampled.
Comparing the two Gram matrices allows individual features to adapt while preserving clean spatial structure.
spec.hint: Select a step to see it drawn out.

steps.label: Dual inputs
steps.title: Feed crops at two resolutions
steps.note: Global crops enter the active student at standard resolution (256x256), while entering the frozen Gram teacher at twice the resolution (512x512). Rotary position embeddings handle the difference.

nodes.label: Global crop
nodes.note: Sampled global crops are passed to both pathways simultaneously.

nodes.label: Student crop
nodes.note: The active student processes the standard 256x256 image crop.

nodes.label: Teacher crop
nodes.note: The frozen Gram teacher receives the same crop at twice the spatial resolution.

steps.label: Features
steps.title: Extract and down-sample patch maps
steps.note: The student outputs patch features at native resolution. The Gram teacher outputs features from double resolution, which are down-sampled by 2x using bicubic interpolation.

nodes.label: Student ViT
nodes.note: The current model being trained with DINO, iBOT, and KoLeo losses.

nodes.label: Gram teacher
nodes.note: An early checkpoint from 100k or 200k steps, held frozen to retain clean spatial properties.

nodes.label: Student map
nodes.note: L2-normalized patch features X_S of dimension P by d.

nodes.label: Down-sampled map
nodes.note: Teacher features down-sampled to P patch vectors matching student dimensions.

steps.label: Gram mats
steps.title: Compute pairwise patch similarities
steps.note: Each patch feature is L2-normalized. Computing dot products across all P patches produces a P-by-P Gram matrix representing internal spatial relations for that crop.

panels.label: Student Gram (X_S X_S^T)
panels.note: Pairwise similarity matrix of student patch vectors. Without anchoring, it becomes noisy.

panels.label: Teacher Gram (X_G X_G^T)
panels.note: Pairwise similarity matrix from the smoothed, high-resolution early teacher.

steps.label: Gram loss
steps.title: Apply Gram loss and update teacher
steps.note: Frobenius norm between both Gram matrices forms the loss, weighted by 2. The Gram teacher is updated to the EMA teacher every 10k iterations.

items: Loss: squared Frobenius norm ||X_S X_S^T - X_G X_G^T||_F^2
Loss weight w_Gram = 2 added to DINO, iBOT, and KoLeo
Gram teacher updated to EMA teacher every 10k iterations

ops.text: You maintain an older frozen checkpoint as the Gram teacher to compute the anchor Gram matrix.
You calculate the student Gram matrix during training and compare it against the anchor matrix using the Gram loss.

args.summary: Integrating Gram anchoring requires maintaining an older checkpoint as a Gram teacher and adding a Gram loss during training to align patch relationships.
